@graph.headline: Win Rate vs Risk-Reward in Trading: Which One Actually Makes You Money?

acceptedAnswer.text: Neither in isolation. Focus on their product — expectancy per trade. A high win rate with a tiny ratio can lose money (60% at 1:0.5 loses), and a big ratio with too low a win rate cannot survive its losing streaks. Evaluate the pair together from your journal, and fix whichever half is weaker.

mainEntity.name: Should I focus on win rate or risk-reward?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — if the ratio compensates. A 30% win rate at 1:3 nets +Rs 2,000 per 100 trades at Rs 100 risk (before costs). The catch is survival: at 30%, a 10-loss streak across 100 trades is about 58% likely (assuming independent outcomes), so your position sizing and psychology must withstand long dry spells. Low win rate strategies pay you for enduring discomfort most traders will not.

mainEntity.name: Can you be profitable with a low win rate?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no universal number — start from the breakeven logic instead. Pick the ratio your setups honestly reach, then ask what win rate it demands: at 1:1 you need above 50%, at 1:1.5 above 40%, at 1:2 above 33.3% — all before costs, so real trading needs a margin above those lines. The honest answer is the pairing you can execute: intraday scalpers typically run 1:0.5 to 1:1 with high win rates, while intraday swing-style traders target 1:1.5 to 1:2. Whatever you choose, compute the ratio on net, after-cost numbers — costs hit small intraday targets hardest — and beware of pasting far-away targets just to claim a big ratio.

mainEntity.name: What is a good risk-reward ratio for day trading?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because the ratio is geometry, not a forecast — a 1:5 plan says nothing about whether price reaches the target. Widening the target lowers the probability of reaching it, which usually lowers your win rate by more than the ratio improves. A ratio only has value if the target is a level price realistically reaches and your realized win rate clears the breakeven threshold for it.
